newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-IRWIN WINS FIFTH SENIOR TOURNAMENT OF THE YEAR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-IRWIN WINS FIFTH SENIOR TOURNAMENT OF THE YEAR.

text.p: Hale Irwin birdied the final two holes on Sunday to break a deadlock with Lee Trevino and win the $1.35 million Burnet Classic for his fifth victory of the year on the Senior Tour.
The two were tied at 15-under heading to the par-3 17th hole. Irwin birdied from 20 feet and Trevino three-putted from 35 feet for bogey, and both players birdied the 18th.

Irwin's final round of 6-under-par 66 enabled him to break the tournament record with a three-round total of 17-under 199 at the 6,909-yard Bunker Hills Golf Club. Chi Chi Rodriguez in 1993 and Ray Floyd in 1995 shared the previous mark.
"It doesn't matter who you play head-to-head," Irwin said. "In that situation, the individual becomes nameless and faceless. It helps to play a guy like Lee in that you know what he is capable of."
By capturing the $202,500 first prize, the 52-year-old Irwin pushed his 1997 earnings to $1,339,561, tops on the tour. Jim Colbert set the Senior Tour record last year with $1,627,890.
Trevino shot 67 and settled for his second runner-up finish of the year at 201. The all-time leader in Senior Tour victories has won just once in the past two years.
"I haven't put three rounds in the 60s together all year," he said. "Hale's the best out here right now. I gave it my best shot. I hit the wrong shot at 17. I hit a 5-iron and should have hit 6."
Senior Players Championship winner Larry Gilbert was third at 204 after closing with a 68, his 22nd consecutive round of par or better.
In 49 career starts on the Senior Tour, Irwin has 22 top-three finishes, including nine victories.
